The answer is correct: Antarctica is the largest desert (~14 million km²), with the Arctic second (~13.9 million km² is the commonly cited figure; some sources say 13.7) and the Sahara the largest hot desert (~9.2 million km²). The definition of a desert by precipitation is the key reasoning. The comparison of the Sahara to the US is accurate (US ~9.8 million km², Sahara ~9.2, so "roughly the size" is fine). The word count is under 120 (about 85). The response is clear and well-formatted, and it addresses the ambiguity in the question.
